Read strings as a Temporal type, with NA for those that fail

Source: R/parse.R
zutempo_parse.Rd

The bulk-reading escape of the string constructors (design 6.8). A constructor such as plain_date() stops at the first string it cannot read; zutempo_parse() reads the rest and returns NA for each string that fails, with the reasons in an attribute.

Usage

zutempo_parse(x, type, ..., na_on_error = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A character vector.

type

The type to read, as the name of its constructor: "plain_date", "plain_time", "plain_date_time", "plain_year_month", "plain_month_day", "instant", "zoned_date_time" or "duration".

...

Options for the constructor, such as disambiguation and offset for "zoned_date_time".

na_on_error

TRUE (the default) returns NA for a string that cannot be read. FALSE raises the constructor's error for the first one, as calling the constructor does.

Value

A vector of the class type names, as long as x. With na_on_error = TRUE it has the attribute "parse_errors": a data frame with one row per failed string, giving its index in x, the 1-based byte position where reading stopped (NA when the string was read but its value was rejected), the condition class and the message.

Details

A string fails when it does not follow the type's ISO 8601 / RFC 9557 grammar, or when it does but names a value the type cannot hold: a date out of range, an unknown time zone, an offset that does not match its zone. Both kinds become NA.

See also

zutempo_parse_errors() to read the attribute.

Examples

x <- c("2026-03-07", "2026-13-01", NA, "2026-02-30")
d <- zutempo_parse(x, "plain_date")
d
#> <zutempo_plain_date[4]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07 <NA>       <NA>       <NA>      
zutempo_parse_errors(d)
#>   index position               class
#> 1     2        6 zutempo_parse_error
#> 2     4        9 zutempo_parse_error
#>                                                                                 message
#> 1    cannot parse "2026-13-01" as a date or date-time: month must be 01 to 12 at byte 6
#> 2 cannot parse "2026-02-30" as a date or date-time: no such day in that month at byte 9
try(zutempo_parse(x, "plain_date", na_on_error = FALSE))
#> Error : cannot parse "2026-13-01" as a date or date-time: month must be 01 to 12 at byte 6 (element 2)
